name: Black Death Reaches Europe
summary: A devastating plague pandemic entered Europe and killed a large share of the population.
details: The Black Death spread rapidly through trade routes, ports, towns, and countryside. Its demographic shock altered labor markets, religious life, social tensions, urban governance, and memory. Europe after the plague was poorer in people but changed in bargaining power and political imagination.
background: The plague moved through commercial and maritime networks linking the Black Sea, Mediterranean ports, and inland towns.
Dense urban populations, trade routes, and limited medical knowledge made Europe highly vulnerable to rapid spread.
aftermath: The demographic shock transformed labor relations, religious life, urban governance, and social tensions across Europe.

contentSections.title: Main events
paragraphs: The demographic shock transformed labor relations, religious life, urban governance, and social tensions across Europe.

The Black Death spread rapidly through trade routes, ports, towns, and countryside. Its demographic shock altered labor markets, religious life, social tensions, urban governance, and memory. Europe after the plague was poorer in people but changed in bargaining power and political imagination.

contentSections.title: Key figures
paragraphs: No commander directed the plague's spread. Key observers include Giovanni Boccaccio in Florence, whose Decameron records the epidemic, and chroniclers at Siena, Avignon, and other affected cities who measured mortality and social collapse.

contentSections.title: Consequences
paragraphs: The demographic shock transformed labor relations, religious life, urban governance, and social tensions across Europe. Labor scarcity gave many peasants and wage workers bargaining power, while elites often tried to restore older obligations through wage controls and harsher laws. The plague also intensified devotional movements, scapegoating, anti-Jewish violence in some regions, and a sharper awareness of death in late medieval culture.

contentSections.title: Historical significance
paragraphs: Black Death Reaches Europe matters because it reveals how medieval authority was made through conflict, ritual, writing, negotiation, and memory.
